data.name: Darshil
data.gender_notes: Darshil is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who can see the divine and the truth. Derived from the Sanskrit word 'darshan' which means 'to see'. The name Darshil carries the meaning “Sight, Vision” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit. Parents who choose Darshil usually hope their child will grow to embody sight, vision and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for a child who is expected to have strong spiritual insight and wisdom.
data.etymology: Darshil belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Sight, Vision.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Darshil total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

historical_references.reference: Darshil was a renowned Jain scholar and monk who lived during the 12th century CE in India. He is known for his work 'Samayasara', which is a commentary on the 'Acharya-kriyasara' of Hemachandra.

Darshil was also a prominent Hindu philosopher and commentator on the works of Adi Shankara, who lived during the 8th century CE. He wrote several commentaries on Shankara's works, including 'Bhashya' on Shankara's commentary on the Bhagavad Gita (known as 'Gaudapada-bhashya').
